articles.title: AI replacing 3rd language in Karnataka high schools? Teachers protest against move
articles.summary: Karnataka teachers protest AI as a third-language substitute in high schools, urging AI as a separate subject and broader recruitment for all languages.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Hundreds of teachers protested at Freedom Park Monday against state govt’s decision to introduce artificial intelligence (AI) as an alternative to the third language in some high schools of the state.In a representation to govt, Deshiya Bhasha Hitarakshana Vedike said the move to introduce AI in school education was welcome, but making it a substitute for the third language would not be appropriate from the perspective of education or Karnataka’s multilingual tradition.“Language and technology are both essential for students,” the forum said, urging the govt to introduce AI as a separate skill-based or elective subject without affecting third-language education.The forum also raised concerns over govt’s July 14 draft notification on the recruitment to teaching posts in state-run high schools.It said the proposed recruitment of language teachers appeared to be restricted to Kannada and English, potentially affecting the teaching of other languages in govt schools.According to the representation, Hindi, Sanskrit, Urdu, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Konkani, Tulu, Malayalam and Arabic have been taught in govt schools for several decades.Restricting the recruitment, it said, could affect students studying these languages as well as employment opportunities for qualified language teachers.It sought three measures: recruitment of high-school teachers for all recognised languages, creation of separate language-teacher posts based on the number of students studying each language, and introduction of AI as a separate subject rather than as a replacement for the third language.The forum said such measures would help preserve Karnataka’s multilingual education system while enabling students to acquire skills in emerging technologies.You Can articles.title: Jayden Daniels to visit with specialists after sustaining dislocated elbow in loss to Cowboys
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels is once again battling a dislocated elbow.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders find themselves in a familiar — and unfortunate — situation after star quarterback Jayden Daniels left Sunday's game with a dislocated left elbow. After undergoing further testing Monday, Daniels will meet with specialists to consult on the injury, Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday.

Quinn added the team won't have a major update on Daniels until those meetings happen. For now, however, the Commanders are not looking to bring in another quarterback.

Daniels sustained the injury on the final play of the first half in a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys . With the Commanders looking to score before halftime, Daniels took a snap from under center, but awkwardly tripped after one of his linemen appeared to step on his foot, knocking him off-balance. As he was going to the ground, Daniels used his left arm to brace himself.

After chucking the ball incomplete, Daniels lay on the turf until he was eventually carted off the field.

It was a gruesome injury, one that caused Tom Brady — who was in the broadcast booth — to utter an expletive live on the air . Brady quickly apologized for swearing.

After the contest, the Commanders head coach revealed Daniels was dealing with a dislocated left elbow. Quinn added that X-rays did not show a fracture, but that Daniels would undergo additional testing Monday.

It's an injury that Daniels has dealt with before. The 25-year-old missed four games last season due to a dislocated left elbow . He returned to action, but reinjured himself in his first game back and was shut down for the rest of the year. Quinn said Monday that surgery was not mentioned last season, with a source telling ESPN that Daniels did not sustain ligament damage last year, which is why surgery was not recommended at the time.

That injury completely derailed what was supposed to be a star-studded second season for the quarterback. As a rookie, Daniels looked like a future superstar. After being selected No. 2 overall from LSU by the Commanders, Daniels threw 25 touchdowns against nine interceptions as a rookie, leading Washington to the playoffs and making the Pro Bowl in his first year.

His numbers took a massive downturn in Year 2 due to various injuries. Daniels started just seven games last season, tossing eight touchdowns against three interceptions.

With those injuries seemingly behind him, Daniels opened the 2026 NFL season looking to get back on track. After a slow start in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles , Daniels rallied late to nearly lead his team to a win.

The quarterback was off to a modest start against the Cowboys before leaving the contest at the end of the first half.

With Daniels once again sidelined, the Commanders will turn to veteran Marcus Mariota in Week 3. The 32-year-old Mariota performed admirably when pressed into action last season, but went just 2-6 in his eight starts.

articles.title: Travis Kelce makes a $1.7 billion investment in his hometown as NFL retirement speculation grows
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce may still have plenty left to give the Kansas City Chiefs, but his growing business interests suggest he is also thinking about life beyo.
articles.body: Travis Kelce may still have plenty left to give the Kansas City Chiefs, but his growing business interests suggest he is also thinking about life beyond football. The 36-year-old tight end has taken a major step into baseball ownership, joining the Cleveland Guardians' ownership group. For Kelce, the investment is more than a financial move. It brings him closer to the city that shaped his life and career.Travis Kelce joins Cleveland Guardians ownership groupKelce's latest venture marks a meaningful homecoming for the NFL star. Born and raised in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, the Chiefs tight end has become part of the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians, a baseball team reportedly valued at $1.7 billion.The investment gives Kelce a new role in professional sports, this time away from the football field. However, he will have to wait until after the 2027 season before he can become a majority owner.For Kelce, the connection runs far deeper than business. Cleveland remains a central part of his identity, and his latest move reflects the lasting bond he shares with his hometown.Speaking about the investment, Kelce said, “I have so much love for this city.“I say it all the time: I’m just a kid from the Heights living the dream.“I credit every good thing in my life to Cleveland and being raised here with the values and the people and the work ethic.“Cleveland Heights is such a diverse and dynamic place. Every friend, neighbor, teacher and teammate – they all made me the man I am today.“It just fueled such a deep appreciation for life and community and service. That mentality of Cleveland against the world runs deep.“I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat to good ownership in my career, and I know the best teams prioritize culture.“Everyone is there to play their role, and right now, I’m here to observe and learn and really to support the team and the city when and where I can.”Travis Kelce's business empire grows as retirement talk buildsThe Guardians investment adds another major name to Kelce's expanding business portfolio. The Chiefs star already holds a stake in the Alpine Formula One team and has interests in an amusement park company, a mattress business, a beer brand and a restaurant. He also co-hosts the New Heights podcast with his brother, Jason Kelce.His baseball investment comes at a time when questions about his NFL future continue to surface. Kelce signed a one-year, $12 million contract with Kansas City for his 14th season, keeping him in the game while retirement speculation follows him.His latest move also comes as he prepares to marry Taylor Swift on July 3. articles.body: Tom Brady is building a future that stretches far beyond the football field. The NFL legend has backed a major funding round for eMed, a digital healthcare company betting on artificial intelligence to reshape employee wellness. The startup has raised $200 million, pushing its valuation above $2 billion. With Brady investing both money and time, the deal adds a new dimension to his growing business interests.Tom Brady backs eMed's $200 million funding roundThe latest funding round puts eMed in a new position within the growing digital healthcare market. The Miami-based company secured $200 million in Series A financing, with its valuation now exceeding $2 billion.Brady, who serves as eMed's founding chief wellness officer, joined a group of prominent investors in the deal. The list includes CEO Linda Yaccarino, former head of X, alongside AON Consulting, Paragon Biosciences founder Jeff Aronin and Valor Equity Partners CEO Antonio Gracias.Other investors include 8VC founder Joe Lonsdale, Chicago Cubs chairman Tom Ricketts and Lettuce Entertain You Restaurants CEO R.J. Melman.For Brady, the investment reflects a personal commitment to the company's vision. He is not simply lending his name to the venture. His role also connects him with its mission to make healthcare more accessible through technology."I believe eMed's empathic agentic AI platform, combined with the strength of its people and partners, represents a true winning formula. Its programmes aim to help employers provide structured care, including support for common side effects associated with GLP-1 treatments.The new funding will help eMed improve its agentic AI platform and prepare for a new capitated care model. The approach is designed to help employers expand access to GLP-1 medications while managing healthcare costs.The company's focus on AI-powered care also places Brady in a sector where technology and preventive health are increasingly connected. articles.title: ‘He Should Not Be Starting,’ ‘What Are We Doing?’ — Buccaneers Fans React to HC Todd Bowles Contradicting Rueben Bain Jr. Over Injury Status
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gotten off to a surprisingly poor start this season. After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, they fell to the Clevela...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gotten off to a surprisingly poor start this season. After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1, they fell to the Cleveland Browns in their home opener in a dreadful performance. Now the Buccaneers sit 0-2, and plenty of panic is spreading among the fanbase.

The Buccaneers need to be better on both sides of the ball, but a few specific players have been called out for low production. One is rookie defensive end Rueben Bain Jr. While it usually takes rookies some time to get acclimated to the NFL, the team needs something from their first-round pick given how much they are struggling on defense.

Buccaneers Fans Critical of Rueben Bain Jr.'s Situation

Bain looked dominant during training camp, and that raised the level of expectation for the rookie in his first season. However, we have not seen the same player in the first two weeks. Bain insists he is not injured, but Bucs head coach Todd Bowles is not convinced.

JoeBucsFan.com reported that "Bain says the shoulder is not affecting his play, per Bowles. However, it sounded like Bowles is skeptical."

"I don't think he's completely healthy," Bowles said of Bain. "But at the same time, he's good enough to play. We've got to get more production there."

For Latest Information: NFL Injury Report

Bowles' comments seem to contradict what the rookie believes about his health, and the team's fans were quick to react to it.

Joshua A. Martin said on X, "If Bain is not healthy, sit him down! He deserves to be out on the field healthy. He clearly isn't the same player as we seen during the preseason/training camp."

One fan wrote, "Then he should not be starting," in reference to Bowles saying Bain isn't fully healthy.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Another fan added, "Currently looks like Walker is better at this point if Bain isn't healthy – WTF we doing here?!"

The Walker referenced is David Walker , the Bucs' fourth-round pick last season. In limited snaps, he recorded a sack against the Browns, and that is more than you can say for Bain.

Evan T on X had a similar response to Bain playing many more snaps than Walker. He said, "David Walker played like what — 3 snaps and had a sack? What are we doing???????"

It seems like Buccaneers fans are fed up with the defensive rotations to begin the season. Most of that is directed at Bowles, a defense-minded head coach who has the final say on who is on the field.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Through two games, the Bucs are giving up 28 points per game, and their defense is ranked 15th on PFN's Defense Impact Metric . That won't cut it, especially for a team whose offense has struggled so far.

The Bucs have plenty of time to turn their season around, but they need more on both sides of the ball. Developing Bain and other rookies will also go a long way toward their being successful.

Naresh said on X, "My big worry is he is not gonna get properly developed because of this Coaching Staff."

Bowles may find himself on the hot seat if he does not turn things around fast. Buccaneers fans aren't used to being uncompetitive, and that is the path they are currently on.

articles.title: The best of the (actually funny) Caleb Williams injury memes
articles.summary: There were some pretty vicious Caleb Williams memes, but others were downright funny. Perhaps even to Caleb himself.
articles.body:
The good news for Bears QB Caleb Williams is that his injured hamstring is about as good as he or the team could have hoped.

The bad news? Social media is roasting Williams' real-time reaction to the injury when it happened. Some are funny. Others are downright vicious, questioning the toughness of the same quarterback who got beat to a pulp as a rookie.

If you watched Williams go down late in Sunday's game, it was a pretty shocking moment. He fell untouched and writhed in pain, unable to get up immediately. Solder Field, already a bit down after a bad offensive day and three hours in the rain, fell silent.

Now that we know Williams' hamstring didn't detach from the bone, it was open season. You knew it was bound to happen.

The Keyboard Corps is really leaning into the same through line on most of these: that being carted off for a short-term injury is a serious affront. Even former NFL players got in on the action.

But we're going to veer away from that type of response. Some of the Williams memes were downright funny. These were jokes that maybe even Williams could possibly laugh at. You know, when he's feeling better. (Watch it!)

It felt like this one was made specifically for my wife.

Anyone who has kids knows this one is good.

I'd rather step on a jellyfish than a Lego piece. Seriously. They're colored caltrops for kids.

Lieutenant Dan had more than a grade-1 hammy.

There actually were multiple "Forrest Gump"-related memes, including this well-worn trope.

This is absurd, but mesmerizingly funny, too.

This one has a whole series, including burning your mouth on a Hot Pocket …

This is just good, clean fun from where I'm sitting.

Williams is going to be asked about this — or these memes — at some point. Maybe it's not this week, as head coach Ben Johnson said Williams might not practice. But eventually, Williams will be asked.

I'll be curious about his reaction to them. There are some parallels to the Paul Pierce situation from a generation ago. In Game 1 of the 2008 NBA Finals, Pierce had to be carried off the floor, yet he miraculously returned in just a few game minutes to make a few buckets and go on to win Finals MVP.

The backstory of that one isn't clear. Did Pierce really use the "injury" as an excuse to use the commode? Maybe, even if Pierce's story has wavered on that one over the years.

If Williams has fun with it, it could turn in his favor. If not? It might be the kind of thing fans hang around his neck for every tough game, every tough playoff loss or — yep — every time he gets hurt in a game.

We'd hate to see that. And you can probably tell, these memes are mostly in the we-all-can-laugh-without-being-mean category. Some are downright terrific.

The rest? Most of us have already moved on from those.

articles.title: Before raising two Super Bowl champions, Donna Kelce faced the challenges of motherhood that shaped the Kelce brothers’ rise to greatnes
articles.summary: NFL News: Long before Donna Kelce became one of the most recognisable mothers in the NFL, her days revolved around work, family responsibilities and two energet.
articles.body: Long before Donna Kelce became one of the most recognisable mothers in the NFL, her days revolved around work, family responsibilities and two energetic boys who rarely sat still. Raising Jason and Travis Kelce brought plenty of challenges, and there was no guarantee either son would reach professional football. Behind their remarkable careers was a mother learning, sacrificing and finding her way through the demanding journey of parenthood.Donna Kelce called motherhood the hardest challenge of her lifeFor Donna Kelce, raising two sons was a very different experience from building a career. The former commercial banker worked hard to support her family, but the responsibilities of motherhood brought a level of uncertainty that no job could match.In an October 2024 interview with Glamour, Donna reflected on the demands of raising Jason and Travis, offering a candid look at the challenges behind her family’s success.“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work,” Donna said.She went on to explain why parenting could feel so overwhelming, especially when children depended on her for almost everything.“But raising children, when they’re totally dependent on you and you’re trying to do the best you can with the limited resources that you have, it’s the most daunting task I’ve ever had to do.”Her words revealed a side of Donna that fans do not always see. Today, she is often celebrated for her sons’ achievements, but her own story includes the everyday pressure of providing for a family while trying to make the right decisions for two growing children.Donna was also a major breadwinner, balancing professional responsibilities with the needs of her family. The experience demanded time, energy and careful choices. Unlike football, where a season eventually ends, motherhood offered no clear finish line.Raising Jason and Travis Kelce meant handling a house full of energyJason and Travis grew up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, where sports became a major part of their lives. But their childhoods were not built around a carefully planned path to the NFL.The brothers tried different sports, including hockey, basketball and lacrosse. Football became a bigger part of their lives later, after they reached seventh grade.Before college recruiters showed interest, Donna was simply raising two active boys. Their energy often kept the household on its toes, and she has recalled the broken windows and calls from neighbours that came with their childhood antics.Still, Donna made a point of explaining that her sons were not bad children. They were lively, competitive and often difficult to keep occupied.In a 2024 interview with Us Weekly, she recalled how important it was to keep the boys busy.“Jason and Travis were very active, and if we wanted any sanity in the household at all, we knew we had to keep them extremely busy,” Donna said.The family also had to consider the cost of keeping up with two children involved in activities. Donna and her former husband, Ed Kelce, had to weigh the financial demands of raising their sons while making sure they had opportunities to explore their interests.Those years may not have looked extraordinary at the time. Yet they helped establish the routine, discipline and family support that became important as Jason and Travis pursued football more seriously.Donna Kelce put respect and kindness ahead of football fameDonna never needed her sons to become NFL stars to feel proud of them. Her focus as a mother was on the people they would become, not just the careers they might build.She has spoken about teaching Jason and Travis to treat everyone with respect, regardless of their position or status. In a 2024 interview with Us Weekly, Donna explained the lesson she wanted her sons to carry into adulthood.“I just wanted to make sure that they treated everyone the same. I said, ‘I don’t care if they’re the individuals who are cleaning the toilets or they’re the CEO of organizations,’” Donna said. “It’s basically, treat everybody with respect, like you would want to be treated.”That principle offered a foundation beyond the football field. Professional sports can bring fame, money and public attention, but Donna wanted her sons to remember that character matters regardless of success.Her approach also meant allowing Jason and Travis to develop their own identities. Their paths were not identical. Jason became a standout centre for the Philadelphia Eagles, while Travis built his career as a tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs.Both reached the highest level of the sport, but their success came through different experiences, decisions and challenges. Donna’s role was not to script their futures. It was to support them as they found their way.The Kelce brothers’ Super Bowl moment made Donna’s sacrifices unforgettableDonna’s years of parenting took on a new meaning when Jason and Travis faced each other in Super Bowl LVII in February 2023. Jason’s Eagles met Travis’ Chiefs, creating the first Super Bowl matchup between two brothers.For Donna, the game presented an emotional dilemma no parent would easily resolve. One son would celebrate a championship, while the other would walk away disappointed.Rather than choosing a side, she wore a split jersey representing both teams. The image quickly became one of the defining moments of that Super Bowl, capturing the pride and conflict of a mother whose sons had reached the same extraordinary stage.The game also brought renewed attention to the family’s journey. Jason and Travis had gone from two energetic boys growing up in Ohio to Super Bowl champions, each with a career that millions of fans followed.Yet Donna’s own reflections make clear that the journey was never just about trophies. She had spent years balancing work, family finances and the unpredictable demands of raising children. She had watched her sons grow, make mistakes, discover their strengths and pursue their ambitions.Jason and Travis’ achievements are theirs, earned through years of effort and commitment. But Donna’s influence remains part of their story, from the values she taught them to the support she offered long before the cameras arrived.For Donna Kelce, the most meaningful reward may not be the Super Bowl rings or the recognition that followed. It is seeing the boys she raised become successful adults, loving fathers and men who still value the family that helped shape them.Sources: Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year interview · Us Weekly’s profile of Donna Kelce · TIME’s interview with Donna Kelce .Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mike Evans Injury Update, Latest on 49ers WR, Fantasy Outlook and Top Waiver-Wire Targets
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Monday that Mike Evans' injured hip will "have to be managed this week" after the veteran wideout left Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins with the issue and didn't return.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Monday that Mike Evans' injured hip will "have to be managed this week" after the veteran wideout left Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins with the issue and didn't return.

Shanahan did suggest on Sunday that Evans' injury wasn't serious.

"It can always change tomorrow," he told reporters after the game. "But if the game was different, he would've been able to come back in."

That was an important update for a Niners team already without De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson at the receiver position, leaving Evans and Deebo Samuel as the top options out wide for Brock Purdy.

It would be good news for fantasy football enthusiasts relying on Evans this season, though if he's forced to miss time, there are options on the waiver wire.

In Las Vegas, Tre Tucker is coming off a fantastic game (five catches for 119 yards and a touchdown), though the potential return of Brock Bowers could limit his targets. Still, he's clearly emerged as Kirk Cousins' preferred target among the team's wideouts.

Monitor Zay Flowers' status in Baltimore. If he misses Week 3, Rashod Bateman—who caught seven passes for 88 yards and a score with Flowers out of the lineup on Sunday—is a good short-term add.

In Philadelphia, Dontayvion Wicks continues to impress as the No. 2 wideout behind DeVonta Smith, putting up seven catches for 147 yards and a score after two games. Expect Jalen Hurts to continue relying on him in the passing game with Dallas Goedert scheduled to be out of action for a few weeks with a strained MCL.

Finally, it appears Denzel Boston has emerged as a trusted target for Deshaun Watson in Cleveland. The rookie second-rounder has seven catches for 154 yards and two touchdowns on the season and is tied with KC Concepcion for the team-lead in targets (11).

Trusting anybody on the Browns never feels great, but Boston is off to a very promising start and is worth your consideration.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy 'committed' to offense built around Aaron Rodgers, points to offensive line play as source of unit's struggles
articles.summary: As long as Pittsburgh's offense remains toothless, McCarthy will continue to field questions about his starting quarterback. At some point, pointing to the o...
articles.body:
Through two games, the Pittsburgh Steelers have one of the worst offenses in the NFL, ranking 30th out of 32 teams with 249.5 yards per game and 30th with 23 total points.

Pittsburgh's defense accounts for seven of those points thanks to a pick 6 by T.J. Watt in Week 1's 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons .

Pittsburgh's offensive woes took center stage Sunday in a listless 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots . The Steelers managed just 235 yards on 3.5 yards per play. They advanced to the red zone once in the game's final minutes and turned the ball over when they got there.

Aaron Rodgers threw one interception and fumbled twice; one was recovered by the Patriots for a scoop-and-score touchdown that iced New England 's win.

Rodgers was under pressure throughout the game and frequently resorted to check downs and short passes when he was able to get rid of the ball while averaging 4.8 yards per attempt. He was sacked four times and hit seven others.

Pittsburgh's running backs were repeatedly met by Patriots defenders at or near the line of scrimmage.

McCarthy 'committed' to plan around Rodgers

On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy was asked frequently about Pittsburgh's offensive struggles during his weekly news conference . Two topics came up repeatedly: Pittsburgh's offensive line and Rodgers.

McCarthy remained steadfast in his support of Rodgers and the value he believes the 42-year-old former four-time MVP brings to the team.

"We have a quarterback that has an incredible wealth of experience," McCarthy said. "And we've built this offense based on his experiences and to play to his strengths. He's knows that, and I'm committed to it."

McCarthy instead pointed to Pittsburgh's offensive line as the primary source of the Steelers' offensive struggles.

"We're a protection-first unit, and that wasn't the case yesterday," McCarthy said. "Our quarterback was hit too much yesterday."

McCarthy took some of the blame of the unit's struggles due to his preseason strategy of rotating players in and out of spots on the offensive line. He believes that the line will improve with more reps together as the season progresses.

"I think in hindsight you go back and you look: how many days did we line up with the same offensive line?" McCarthy said. "We worked a lot of different combinations. No excuses, but they need continuity.

"They need reps, they need consistency. So the consistency will come through the common concepts."

In an ideal football world, an NFL unit isn't going into Week 3 of the regular season without enough reps to have cohesion. Pittsburgh's offensive line struggles are real and playing a significant impact on the unit's slow start.

Will McCarthy hold Rodgers accountable for poor play?

But that doesn't address the questions around Rodgers. At 42 years old with an Achilles tendon that's been repaired, Rodgers isn't remotely close to the form that led him to four MVPs and a Super Bowl title with the Green Bay Packers . He hasn't been for years.

Rodgers won that Super Bowl with McCarthy as his head coach, and the two have a relationship built on those objectively better times. For now, McCarthy remains firmly in Rodgers' corner in his first year as Pittsburgh's head coach.

But as long as Pittsburgh's offense remains toothless, McCarthy will continue to field questions about his starting quarterback. At some point, if this continues, pointing to the offensive line won't be a satisfactory answer.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart has reportedly suffered a sprained MCL, with Ian Rapoport of NFL Network providing additional details:

Head coach John Harbaugh discussed the injury after the game:

Dart exited Monday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams in the first quarter after taking a big hit in the pocket. He suffered a left knee injury and was taken to the locker room after staying down on the field for some time before walking off under his own power.

Dart was eventually ruled out of the game with a knee injury, although general manager Joe Schoen had a positive outlook:

Despite the injury, he reportedly wanted to go back into the game:

As a rookie in 2025, Dart provided excitement and hope for a struggling franchise. He took over the reins of the offense in Week 4 and completed 63.7 percent of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions in 12 starts. He also rushed for 487 yards and nine touchdowns.

The No. 25 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft has unfortunately taken some big hits, though, and one of them led to a concussion against the Chicago Bears last Nov. 16 that cost him the next two games.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan provided the details: "Dart took a hard hit on a fumble in the third quarter, getting hit from the side as he ran by a defensive lineman tracking back to make the play. His head hit the ground, and he got up slowly, eventually walking to the sideline after remaining on the field for a few seconds on his knees. Dart returned to the game the following drive for two plays and then went to the blue medical tent in between quarters. He walked slowly into the locker room afterward with a trainer. The first-round pick was ruled out later in the fourth quarter."

Dart is the present and future in New York as the Giants look to break a malaise that's seen the team post losing records 11 times in 13 seasons.

New York does have a solid backup quarterback though in Jameis Winston, who led the offense to success last season against the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions while Dart was out.

Over those two starts, Winston threw for 567 yards and two touchdowns (two interceptions) while adding a rushing touchdown as well as a receiving score on a trick play in the Detroit game.

articles.title: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffers knee injury against Rams, possible MCL issue feared
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart injured his left knee on a high-low hit during Monday Night Football, and the New York Giants are now evaluating a possible MCL issue.
articles.body: The optimism and good tidings the New York Giants enjoyed through the first week of the NFL season are suddenly on hold as the team is busy evaluating the status of injured quarterback Jaxson Dart. Dart, in his second NFL season, injured his left knee during the first series of the Monday Night Football game between the Giants and Los Angeles Rams. The injury happened on a first-quarter hit when Dart was hit by Rams defenders both high and low. And the low hit seemed to cause his left knee to bend in a manner it is not meant to bend. That's not all. The team also had a bit of a scare when receiver Malik Nabers left the game after a pass thrown his way fell incomplete. He was seen clutching his right shoulder. JOHN HARBAUGH AND JAXSON DART AIM TO PULL THE NEW YORK GIANTS OUT OF THE NFC EAST BASEMENT Nabers returned after missing a couple of series nursing his shoulder on the bench. The hit on Dart left the quarterback on the ground clutching at the knee of his forward leg when he throws. That is never a good sign. The saving grace: Dart's leg was not planted on the turf when he was hit. PATRICK MAHOMES ANSWERS TROUBLING QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS SERIOUS KNEE INJURY ON FIRST DRIVE OF THE CHIEFS SEASON That allowed the entire part of the lower leg to bend with the knee. So, this is not a season-ending ACL tear. MALIK NABERS REVEALS HOW GIANTS COACH JOHN HARBAUGH HELPED HIM OVERCOME HIS ACL INJURY FEARS But Dart suffered some sort of MCL issue, according to an NFL source. If that is confirmed by an MRI scheduled for Tuesday. "Yeah, we'll know more tomorrow," coach John Harbaugh said after the game. "That's in the neighborhood of it, I would say. We'll get an MRI tomorrow and have a really good feel for it, and it'll give you more information then." Dart won't need surgery, but will miss some time. This is not, however, a season-ending injury. "The fact that it's not that outcome that you're talking about, the devastating outcome, is really good news," Harbaugh said. Dart limped off the field and was initially treated in the team's medical tent. Several teammates huddled outside the medical tent while Dart was inside, no doubt worried about the status of their starting quarterback. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston came on in his absence and was largely ineffective, throwing one interception without a touchdown and posting a passer rating of 37.7, which is bad. articles.title: Darius Slayton, Colts Reportedly Agree to Contract Amid Alec Pierce Injury, Latest Fantasy Impact
articles.summary: After being released by the New York Giants before the start of the season, Darius Slayton is back on an NFL roster.
articles.body:
After being released by the New York Giants before the start of the season, Darius Slayton is back on an NFL roster.

Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts signed the veteran receiver on Monday after Alec Pierce suffered a heel injury against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday.

Slayton spent the first seven years of his career with the Giants, racking up 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns. In 2025, he had 538 yards and a touchdown in 14 games.

With New York adding Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr. this offseason, the release of Slayton wasn't all that surprising. The Giants also saved over $3 million in cap space by releasing him.

Now, he'll get the chance to reunite with Daniel Jones in Indianapolis. Slayton's best seasons came when he was catching passes from Jones, and he'll look to get back to his best form with the Colts.

As for how big a role he'll play in Indianapolis, that depends on how long Piece is out. According to Joel A. Erickson of the Indianapolis Star, Pierce is "likely" going to be out for several weeks, so the Colts will need some players to step up in the meantime.

Josh Downs will presumably be Jones' first option, and he played well after Pierce's exit on Sunday, catching seven passes for 72 yards in the overtime loss to the Chiefs.

Keenan Allen will likely get more targets as well, and Indianapolis will need to rely on tight end Tyler Warren more in the coming weeks. Slayton will certainly have the chance to play a big role, but he might not be worth fantasy managers picking up just yet.

He'll look to settle in with the Colts over the next week before potentially making his debut against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

articles.title: Rams Beat Giants amid Dart Injury, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Stafford, Adams, Skattebo, More
articles.summary: Look away, New York Giants fans. Just look away.
articles.body:
Look away, New York Giants fans. Just look away.

On a night when Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury and didn't return and Malik Nabers suffered a shoulder injury and did return (but barely made an impact), the Giants were no match for the Los Angeles Rams, losing 28-6.

Here's a look at the stats for the key players from both sides:

Much of the intrigue surrounding the game resides with Dart and the severity of his injury. He reportedly wanted to return to the game, potentially a good sign that the injury won't be a serious one.

But on the field, the main story was Adams, who absolutely torched the New York secondary from the jump. With Puka Nacua out for a hip injury—and the Rams still smarting from a 27-7 loss against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia to start the season—it was a much-needed performance.

That Matt Stafford guy was pretty good too.

The Rams' front four also completely dominated on the other side of the ball, harassing Winston into a rough performance. Aaron Donald also made his season debut and looked good.

Overall, Monday night was exactly what the Rams needed after a humbling start to the 2026 season. For the Giants, on the other hand, it was an unmitigated disaster, with the hope that it will be contained to one night.

Up next for the Rams is a trip to Denver to face the Broncos next Sunday night, while the Giants will host the Tennessee Titans in the early slate.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 3: Are the Vikings the best team in the NFC North?
articles.summary: The Vikings are off to a great 2-0 start to this season.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

A wellness check on the NFC North after two weeks doesn't give particularly optimistic results. The Detroit Lions ' defense is in major trouble and the issues might not be easily fixable. The Chicago Bears ' defense isn't much better, and the offense feels a little more vulnerable after scoring only three points in Week 2. The Green Bay Packers ' defense has been average but the offense might be falling apart at the seams.

The Vikings are undefeated despite getting 11 snaps from Kyler Murray so far this season. He is expected to return from a concussion in Week 3 . At this point it might not matter who the quarterback is.

The Vikings allowed three points to a Bears offense that was the talk of the NFL after scoring 59 in Week 1. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is proving to be a mad scientist. He blitzed Caleb Williams on 27 of his 33 dropbacks (81.8%), according to Next Gen Stats. A week ago, the Vikings blitzed on 40 of Jordan Love 's 46 dropbacks (86.9%), according to Pro Football Focus. At this point opponents should assume Flores is blitzing at about an 80% rate, which is astonishing in the NFL. But it has been successful.

The Vikings' offense hasn't been good. It's last in the NFL in yardage gained. But presumably Murray will be better than Carson Wentz . And the Vikings are 2-0 with both wins coming in division games already as their offense catches up.

There's a lot of season to go, but the Vikings are in good shape. Don't forget they were 14-3 two seasons ago with competent quarterback play and 9-8 last season without it. Perhaps everyone should have taken the Vikings more seriously coming into the season. If Murray can play at an average level, perhaps Minnesota is surprisingly the best team in the NFC North? They're certainly in the best shape early this season, even if by default.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 2 of the NFL season:

The Dolphins are the only team in the NFL that has not led at any point through the first two weeks of the season, according to Doug Clawson of CBS . On Sunday, they trailed the 49ers 35-6 before a meaningless touchdown in the final three minutes. The Dolphins were fairly competitive in the first half, trailing just 14-6 at halftime, but were outscored 21-0 in the third quarter.

"We didn't coach well enough in the second half," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said . "We didn't play well enough. I thought we had a great week of preparation. I thought we were ready to play better. Second half, not good enough in any phase."

The Dolphins' next three games are against 2-0 teams: vs. Chiefs , at Vikings, vs. Bengals .

The Falcons' passer rating through two games is 38.2. If a team threw incomplete on every single play, their passer rating would be 39.6. Michael Penix Jr. has not been a good quarterback yet in his young career, but compared to what the Falcons have put on the field there might be a parade in Atlanta upon the news that he'll start this week against the Packers . Perhaps Penix will play well. He'll certainly be better than Cooper Rush or Jack Strand, and he'll make Atlanta at least watchable on offense. The Falcons play their next three games in prime time for some reason, including Thursday night at Green Bay. There's a lot of time for the Falcons to salvage their season, but it's overly optimistic to believe Penix is a savior. Atlanta's biggest problem has been quarterback, but it's not the only problem.

The Titans aren't in the business for moral victories, but at least they were way more competitive in Week 2 against a talented Eagles team. They led until the Eagles scored the game-winning touchdown with nine seconds left. There will be many regrets. The Titans had first-and-goal at the 9-yard line with 2:37 left on the clock and the game tied, and right tackle JC Latham got immediately beat by Jalen Carter for a 9-yard sack. Tennessee settled for a field goal, giving the Eagles an opening to steal the win. At least everything looked better, including Cam Ward (13 of 20, 183 yards) against a very good defense.

"I think what encouraged me the most was that we were able to get some explosive offense," Ward said .

The Cardinals' longest reception Sunday was 9 yards. That's a stat about the Seahawks more than anything, but it was the first time since Oct. 11, 1987 that the Cardinals didn't complete a pass for at least 10 yards, via Theo Mackie of the Arizona Republic . That game came with replacement players during a player strike. That won't be Arizona 's offense all season, but it is weird how the Cardinals refuse to use Jeremiyah Love more. The third overall pick of the NFL Draft had nine carries for 29 yards, Tyler Allgeier has 22 carries this season and Love has 20. Love might be limited due to a high ankle sprain in preseason, but it makes very little sense why the Cardinals would use that kind of draft capital on a running back and then underutilize him. There's hope for Love emerging, which might not the case for Marvin Harrison Jr. , who has one catch in two games.

There wasn't a great chance that Geno Smith was going to drive the Jets for a win in 50 seconds if Aaron Glenn called a timeout and forced the Packers to punt near the end of regulation. But his explanation, that he was worried about being pinned deep after a punt, doesn't make much sense either.

The Jets are clearly better than last season. They won at a Titans team that was much more competitive in Week 2 against the Eagles, and they led the Packers 17-7 in the fourth quarter. They held the Packers to 199 yards and that counts overtime. But the Jets need to close these games out or Glenn's job security will continue to be an ongoing conversation.

It's strange to see Dan Quinn get criticized for Jayden Daniels dislocating his elbow on the final play of the first half because he went for the touchdown and not the field goal. Going for the touchdown at the 1-yard line when you trail 17-10 is a reasonable football decision. What's unreasonable is calling a game worried about your quarterback getting hurt every play. What happened to Daniels was unfortunate but that's football. The tough part is it's quickly becoming a big part of Daniels' career arc. Since a historic rookie season he played just seven games last season and now is dealing with a dislocated elbow again. The Commanders are 0-2, looked bad on defense against the Cowboys, and now might have to try to save their season with Marcus Mariota presumably filling in for Daniels for a bit.

The last time a team had a start to the season like the Chargers, it was 1926 and that team disbanded one game later. More on those 1926 Racine Tornadoes and the history they now share with the 2026 Chargers, from OptaSTATS:

You don't need 100-year-old comparisons to see the Chargers have been the NFL's most disappointing team so far this season. While one of Justin Herbert 's interceptions Sunday came on a dropped pass that was batted in the air, he has two touchdowns and three interceptions to start the season. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel hasn't transformed the offense as expected. And now the Chargers have a brutal upcoming schedule . A 2-7 midseason record — or worse — is not off the table.

"I'm angry, but being angry doesn't fix anything," Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. said . "Being angry doesn't fix the problem that we have. We have to get it fixed."

The Buccaneers were 6-2 at their bye week last season, and had a win at Seattle on their résumé. They are 2-9 since and one win came last season against a Cardinals team that went 3-14 last season. Sunday's loss to a Browns team that lost to Jacksonville 34-10 the week before is a new low for Todd Bowles, who suddenly has to be the top candidate to be the first head coach fired this season. The Buccaneers are too talented to lose nine of 11 games since the middle of last season.

"We've dealt with adversity before," Bowles said, via the team's site . "This is an adverse situation again, first time at the beginning of the season but we're 0-2 right now. We've got to pull ourselves up by our boots and we've got to win."

If that seemed like Deshaun Watson 's greatest moment with the Browns, it was, statistically speaking. It was his top EPA per dropback in any game for Cleveland.

Watson had a good second half with the Browns' running game doing nothing. Removing Watson's 22 yards on seven rushes, the Browns rushed for 22 yards on 16 carries. Watson and the Browns' defense were the drivers of this win. Watson clearly did enough to keep his job for another week , and the reaction to him from Browns fans at the home opener will be interesting. At least it's coming off a win and a good performance.

The Steelers' offense was bad against the Patriots and afterward, Aaron Rodgers had what was perceived as a bit of a shot at his coaches.

"In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better and it starts with me," Rodgers said . "At, like, making sure Mike [McCarthy] knows what's working, what's not working, our coaches know, so we can call stuff we feel like has a better chance."

Even if his words are being twisted, the big problem is the Steelers are trusting a 42-year-old quarterback way too much. The Steelers have 81 passing attempts, which is third in the league, and they're passing about 65% of the time despite not being in pass-only mode much of the season. The Steelers never trailed by more than four points in Week 1 and the game didn't get away from them Sunday until a Rodgers fumble was returned for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Mike McCarthy has just made a decision to pass it over and over like it's 2011 with Rodgers. Pittsburgh has one offensive touchdown in eight quarters with that approach.

Bryce Young is second in the NFL with 648 passing yards through two games, only 14 yards behind Tyler Shough for the league lead. Young was also tied for first in the NFL through Sunday's games with six touchdown passes. It has helped to play hapless defenses like the Bears and Falcons, but the production is undeniable. It helps that Jalen Coker was one of five receivers through Sunday's games with more than 200 yards through two weeks. Young is under contract through the 2027 season, and he's starting to make a case for the Panthers to give him a lucrative second contract.

The question is whether Shane Steichen should have gone for it in overtime. In hindsight, giving the ball to Patrick Mahomes when all he needed was a field goal to win was not the right call. But it wasn't an easy call. The Colts had a fourth-and-8 and came out hoping to go for it but got a defensive look that was not conducive to them getting the first down. So Steichen called timeout and took the field goal, hoping his defense could get a stop.

Steichen said he told quarterback Daniel Jones , before the timeout: "If you love it, man, let's go at it. Let's go win this thing. But if it's not the right look ... let's kick the field goal here."

He'll be second-guessed for it after the Colts lost a hard-fought game in overtime. Steichen is under a lot of pressure to show progress and keep his job, and an 0-2 start with a questionable coaching decision isn't an ideal beginning.

Nothing looks good for the Packers right now, especially on offense. The line is beyond banged up and Green Bay lost right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele to a potentially season-ending injury. Receiver Jayden Reed went down with a back injury on the Packers' first drive Sunday. The running game is non-existant without Josh Jacobs . MarShawn Lloyd has been a non-factor and got just six carries Sunday before he was essentially benched after a fumble. Jordan Love had just 145 passing yards against a Jets secondary that was historically bad last season and didn't have Minkah Fitzpatrick . The Packers won in overtime Sunday, coming back from a 17-7 fourth-quarter deficit. If they didn't rally, the panic would be ramped up even more. The Packers are lucky the hapless Falcons are next on the schedule because they have a lot of issues to work through.

The Texans ' run game was dreadful Sunday when it had to carry the offense with receiver Nico Collins out. The Texans had a putrid 6.7% success rate on runs against the Bengals. Only one team has a mark under 20% in a game this season, and that was the Raiders at 18.5% in Week 2. It's stunning that the Texans have not fixed their offensive line issues over multiple offseasons despite it being an obvious liability.

"For us just collectively as a team, the one key to this victory was controlling the front and from an offensive perspective and we did not control their front," Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire. "We got outplayed up front. We couldn't run the ball well. That forced us into a lot of passing situations."

The Texans bounced back from an 0-3 start to make the playoffs last season, but they're in a big hole after losing two home games to begin this season.

Klint Kubiak's offense will get a lot of credit for the Raiders' 2-0 start. While that side of the ball is playing well, it's more notable what Vegas' defense is doing. The Raiders' defense is first in the NFL in EPA allowed per play, and by a wide margin . Part of that (and part of the reason the Raiders aren't higher in the rankings yet) is they've played a Dolphins team that might be on 0-17 watch and a Chargers team that has looked as bad as anyone through two weeks. If the Raiders keep playing like this on both sides of the ball, they'll move up fast. And already, it seems like the free-agent and draft additions have made significant improvements on both sides of the ball.

That's more of what we expected from the Cowboys. Dak Prescott threw four touchdowns, breaking Tony Romo 's franchise record for career TD passes . The offense came alive but the defense is still a question after giving up 389 yards despite Jayden Daniels missing half of the game due to an elbow injury. The Cowboys didn't have a sack. They have two sacks in two games, and the only player with more than a half-sack is safety Caleb Downs . Things will be fine if the Cowboys' offense is putting up 37 points like Dallas did Sunday, but it's hard to win that way in the NFL. It's easier to attack those issues after a win, and team owner Jerry Jones is optimistic.

"We're better than we've been in the last two years on defense," Jones said, according to the team's site . "And offensively, we saw some really impressive things tonight."

The Giants had a scare when Jaxson Dart hurt his knee Monday , and while Jameis Winston is one of the better backup quarterbacks in the NFL, he is also capable of throwing his team out of any game with inopportune interceptions. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that initial exams on Dart indicated he has a sprained MCL, which could cause him to miss some time. If he does, the Giants will be much more volatile. Monday night's loss at the Rams was ugly, as the Giants were outgained 481-182, but losing Dart early affected the whole operation. We shouldn't forget how good they looked against the Cowboys in Week 1.

The Saints are a 2-point conversion away from being 2-0 with road wins over the Lions and Ravens . Given the issues elsewhere in the NFC South, the Saints look like they're the best team in the division. They were the best team in the division over the second half of last season too. There was controversy over whether Tyler Shough scored on a fourth-and-goal quarterback sneak that gave the Saints the lead — it was ruled a touchdown on the field though it wasn't clear Shough broke the plane and was not reversed after a replay review — but the comeback in the fourth quarter on the road against a good Ravens team made it a well-earned win. The next step for New Orleans is not falling behind early and having to make a big comeback.

The fear over Caleb Williams' injury has subsided since it seems like a fairly minor hamstring injury, and yes his extremely distressed reaction to a hamstring strain was odd. At least it wasn't a major injury. What needs to be addressed is how the Bears' offense was inept just one week after putting up 59 points at Carolina. The Bears scored three points against Minnesota and that was with Williams playing three-and-a-half quarters. It would have been better had it not been for a D'Andre Swift fumble at the 1-yard line and a blocked field goal. The rainy weather was certainly an issue, but it's not like the Bears won't be playing more bad weather games. They're still having trouble getting Luther Burden III , Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland (14 combined catches in two games) involved. One bad game doesn't mean the Bears are in trouble on offense, but one great game might not make them the highest scoring offense in NFL history either.

"The weather was a major factor in this game," Bears head coach Ben Johnson said, according to the team's site . "It was the big story of this game. Both defensive coordinators did a great job making it very challenging for the opposing offense. I thought that was the tale of the tape."

The Lions have given up 658 passing yards, which is second-most in the NFL, with only the Colts being worse. They are decimated due to injuries, which is why they were working out defensive backs like Jordan Fuller and Jalen Mills on Monday, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Safety Avonte Maddox is the latest to go down; he'll miss the rest of the season due to a foot injury. Since halftime of the season opener, the Lions have given up 71 points and 804 yards. Facing Josh Allen in Week 2 factors into the defensive problems, but it's still alarming.

"Defensively, we knew it was a tall task, but we gave up too much," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said . "There were some things in there that we have to get cleaned up. You have to play your best ball to have a chance to reduce points against that team and that quarterback, and we did not do that. We had a hand in helping them out there a little bit, and it wasn't good enough. It's not good enough."

The good news is the Lions still have an easy schedule, and there are winnable games coming up against the Jets, Panthers and Cardinals. Detroit needs to win those games to quell some fears, especially about its defense.

The Broncos' turnaround after six poor quarters to start the season might have been as simple as figuring out how to get Jaylen Waddle and Jonah Coleman involved. Waddle was mostly invisible in Week 1 with just 2 yards, but he had 138 in Week 2. He won't go off like that every week, but that should be closer to his normal production. Coleman, a rookie, took advantage of injuries to JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey and had 39 yards rushing and 19 yards receiving, and generally looked good. It could become difficult for the Broncos to keep him off the field. The offensive output from Waddle and Coleman, and a much-improved effort from the defense, led to a win over the Jaguars that avoided what would have been a miserable 0-2 start.

"When the sky was falling, I was like, 'Look, this is correctable,'" defensive lineman Zach Allen said, via the team's site .

The Patriots won and they got some downfield passing going, but Drake Maye is still in a slump. He didn't throw a touchdown Sunday and had only 208 yards. His Week 1 struggles can be excused because the Seahawks' defense is incredible. The Steelers' defense isn't on that level and the Patriots were still underwhelming on offense. The Patriots are still figuring out their receiver rotation without A.J. Brown, but the passing offense needs to do more. Maye is 19th in adjusted EPA per play and 10th in success rate, which isn't that bad considering half of his season so far was against Seattle, but it's nowhere near his MVP form of last season.

"You got to be excited and enjoy the win," Maye said, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein . "But at the same time, you realize that playing like this isn't going to end up with offensively us leading our team to wins."

Edge rusher Dallas Turner seems to be having a breakout in his third season. He leads the NFL in pressures (20), QB hits (8) and PFF's pass rush productivity score. With the Bears at the 12-yard line, trailing 9-3, Turner had a sack on the final play of the game to seal the win. Turner was the 17th pick of the 2024 NFL Draft and he is playing up to that draft status.

"DT being our closer, finishing the whole thing," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said after Sunday's win . "DT just keeps showing up."

The Eagles needed to stop a 2-point conversion to beat the Commanders and a last-minute drive with a touchdown in the final seconds to beat the Titans. Those are two of the worst teams in the NFL so far. Life is better at 2-0 but it still has been an uneven start for the Eagles. It's not just an offense learning a new scheme either. The defense is just 22nd in EPA per play allowed and 14th in success rate allowed. The offense is 14th in EPA per play and 27th in success rate. It has been a very mediocre team that made the plays it needed to win two close games. It's early in the season and 2-0 is obviously fine, but don't ignore these warning signs.

There's nothing wrong with losing on the road to a desperate Broncos team. It's tough in the altitude early in the season, and that might have played a factor in the Jaguars blowing a 13-3 second-half lead. Between last season and Week 1, the Jaguars have earned the benefit of the doubt that they're still a very good team despite one loss to a team that went 14-3 last season. One shining light is that receiver Parker Washington has carried over a strong finish from last season. Washington is second in the NFL in target share to only Jaxon Smith-Njigba, according to PFF . Washington is getting 37.5% of the targets despite some good receiver teammates around him. He has turned that into 18 catches for 181 yards through two games. Washington is a rising star.

Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews both had productive days, but the Ravens missed Zay Flowers in their home loss to the Saints. The Ravens were ahead 17-9 but couldn't put the game away in the fourth quarter and lost in the final two minutes. Taking a deep shot on third-and-1 in a tie game rather than handing it to Derrick Henry didn't work and has been criticized. This type of loss has become a flaw for Baltimore. The Ravens have a league-leading 15 losses after they held a double-digit lead since 2018, the team's site said . That's disappointing but there are positive signs for the Ravens through two weeks. They just need to get their receiver room healthy and do a much better job closing games.

"This is a different team [with] different energy," Andrews said, according to transcripts . "This is not par for the course. We are going to learn from this and continue to be better and capitalize when we need to capitalize."

Kenneth Walker might have the second-biggest impact of anyone in the NFL through two weeks, behind Josh Allen. In Week 1, Walker set a career best by forcing 14 missed tackles. In Week 2, he forced 15 missed tackles . When the Chiefs needed a game-winning drive in overtime, he was involved in five of their six offensive plays. Included in that was a 22-yard gain on a catch that got the Chiefs into easy field-goal range. For the first time in a while, the Chiefs have balance on offense and that's helping Patrick Mahomes.

"It's fun for me, just him running the ball, our offensive line driving off the ball the way that they're driving off," Mahomes said . "It's making defenses have to account for that. I mean, if not, we're going to run the ball for 200 yards or whatever we did the week before, and so you want to be able to do it all."

Is Cincinnati's defense good? It was impressive against Houston. The Bengals paid a big price for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II, giving up the 10th overall pick of the draft to the Giants for him. It looks like he might be worth it. Lawrence had a fantastic game Sunday, including a huge fourth-down stop on RB David Montgomery. The Bengals completely shut down the Texans' run game and Lawrence was the biggest element in that.

The Bengals are fourth in EPA allowed per play. If the defense is going to play anywhere near that level, everyone knows the offense is going to heat up and be among the NFL's best. This is the mix the Bengals have been looking for.

It wasn't outrageous to worry a little about Matthew Stafford after a really poor outing for him in Week 1. He is 38 years old, after all. After Rich Gannon won his first MVP at age 37, like Stafford did last season, he threw only nine more touchdowns the rest of his career. But Monday night looked like vintage Stafford, with 327 yards and four touchdowns. That was without Puka Nacua, who was inactive with a hip injury. The entire performance by the Rams should ease any concerns that might have come up when they were dominated by the 49ers in Australia.

"Obviously we executed at a higher clip, had some explosive plays, which is nice," Stafford told ESPN's Lisa Salters after the game. "To be honest with you, I felt like we could have been more efficient. We had some plays we left out there that I know we can make."

The 49ers got a good runout to start the season. They got the Rams in Australia, when Los Angeles practically blew off that trip by landing the day before the game. Then they got the Dolphins, who have the worst roster in the NFL. They blew out both teams, which shouldn't be taken for granted in the NFL. Their point differential of +42 is dominant. They have had only two negative plays all season, not counting kneeldowns, the fewest for a team this century through two games, according to Doug Clawson of CBS . Brock Purdy is playing well, keeping the offense afloat despite receiver injuries already piling up, and the defense has given up only one touchdown to the Rams and another TD to the Dolphins when they were leading by 29 points in the final minutes. It has been an impressive start.

"Obviously, the scoreboard's been great the last two weeks, but there are so many things we can always get better at and our standard is going to continue to rise," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said, via 49ers Web Zone . "That's really what we're focused on."

The Seahawks' defense might be even better than last season, and last season's group was phenomenal. Seattle has allowed 17 points in two games. The Seahawks didn't allow a catch longer than 9 yards against the Cardinals in Week 2 and only one run of 10 yards or longer. On the offensive end, Sam Darnold missed Sunday's game and the running game is still in a weird spot with Jadarian Price not fully taking over the RB1 job. It didn't matter because Jaxon Smith-Njigba was fantastic, with 155 yards and three touchdowns.

"We're sitting over there on the sideline, and when he catches the ball, we're just like, 'Man, this guy's a wizard,'" defensive tackle Leonard Williams said about JSN, via the team's site .

It seems like Josh Allen has simply decided that he's going to have a historic season . Allen has at least two passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns in each game to start the season. That's only the second time in NFL history a player has scored multiple rushing and passing touchdowns in consecutive games. The first time was Allen in 2024, according to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press . Having a healthy Dalton Kincaid seems to have unlocked a new level in the offense. Kincaid has played well at times but injuries have held him back. Now that he's healthy, he's third in the NFL with 225 receiving yards. Assuming DJ Moore's shoulder injury isn't serious, there's no reason Allen can't set career-high marks this season. And we're talking about a player who has accounted for at least 39 touchdowns in six straight seasons.

articles.title: Giants QB Jaxson Dart reportedly believed to have sprained MCL vs Rams
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart went down holding his knee on the Giants' first possession.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is believed to have sustained a sprained MCL in the first quarter of Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams based on initial exams of his injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports .

Per the report, X-rays were negative, and Dart is slated to undergo an MRI for further evaluation Tuesday. While still a significant injury on top of a tough loss to the Rams, the report that arrived at the end of the game was relatively good news for Dart and the Giants.

Head coach John Harbaugh declined to confirm the report postgame, but told reporters "that's in the neighborhood of it" when asked if Dart had sustained a sprained MCL. Harbaugh said he wanted to wait for the results of Dart's MRI before speaking further on the diagnosis.

Dart's injury looked serious as soon as it happened, and it prompted the Giants to send him for in-game X-rays that ultimately didn't reveal a fracture. Dart was on the sideline in street clothes after halftime and walked off the field with his team after the loss without a notable limp.

The late-game report didn't include a prognosis or timeline for Dart's recovery and return to the field. More will be known after Tuesday's MRI. But Dart and the Giants are certainly hoping that all signs point to the injury being less serious than initially feared.

The injury took place on New York's first drive of the game on a third-down pass. Dart was under pressure and jumped to throw downfield. He was hit hard as he was sandwiched between multiple players and injured his left knee.

Dart grabbed his knee in pain. Harbaugh came out to check on him as ESPN went to commercial. Dart got up and limped off the field without assistance. The Giants ruled Dart out early in the third quarter, but ESPN reported that Giants general manager Joe Schoen said about Dart : "He's going to be OK."

Jameis Winston took over at quarterback for the Giants after Dart exited. Dart walked to the locker room as that series began.

The Giants listed Dart as questionable to return initially, and he was later carted to get X-rays. Dart later returned to the sideline in street clothes. ESPN's Jordan Raanan reported that Dart wanted to return to the game.

Dart was a first-round draft pick last year and had a promising rookie season. His aggressiveness and running style led to injury concerns, including being evaluated for concussions five times. The Giants are now left to wait for the result of Tuesday's MRI to have a firmer grasp on his latest injury.

Winston struggled to move New York's offense in Dart's place Monday night as the Rams went on to a dominant win. Both teams are now 1-1.

articles.title: These young quarterbacks were supposed to break out. Now they’re hurt.
articles.summary: The New York Giants’ Jaxson Dart on Monday became the latest upstart QB to be sidelined with an injury, joining the Bears’ Caleb Williams and the Commanders’ Jayden Daniels as signal callers who had to leave the field early in Week 2.
articles.body: The New York Giants were one of the NFL’s pleasant surprises in Week 1, beginning the John Harbaugh era with an impressive win over the Dallas Cowboys thanks in large part to the play of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart. The Giants’ dreams of a turnaround season quickly hit a roadblock on Monday, however, as Dart became the latest upstart QB to be sidelined with an injury. Only two weeks into the NFL season, the game’s young stars are seeing their seasons upended due to varying degrees of injuries. Dart joined the Chicago Bears’ Caleb Williams and the Washington Commanders’ Jayden Daniels as signal callers who had to leave the field early in Week 2. That trio joined a list of sidelined quarterbacks that also includes the Minnesota Vikings’ Kyler Murray and the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks’ Sam Darnold. All five of those players are former first-round draft picks — and all are under the age of 30. Dart left in the first quarter of New York’s 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. On a third-and-8 pass attempt, Dart was sandwiched by multiple players as the pocket collapsed around him, and he took a substantial hit to his left knee from a Rams linebacker. Dart limped off the field and was taken back to the locker room. After initially being ruled questionable to return, he was ruled out for good in the second half. “He’s going to be OK,” Giants general manager Joe Schoen told ESPN’s Laura Rutledge during the “Monday Night Football” broadcast, adding that Dart would undergo X-rays at the stadium. Dart’s hard-charging play style raised eyebrows during his rookie season, when he missed time due to a concussion but seemingly refused to tone down his aggressiveness when he returned. During the preseason, Dart even expressed confusion at why he so often is required to enter the blue medical tent on the sidelines. “I really respect the rules, and the thought behind, you know, the NFL has of keeping players healthy and reviewing things,” Dart said in August after a big hit required he undergo a mandatory medical evaluation. “But at the same time, I’m still puzzled by just feeling like every time that I get hit, you know, I just find my way in there.” Dart’s injury Monday, though, came on a relatively routine pass play, highlighting how no quarterback is ever truly safe. The same can be said of the Commanders’ Daniels, who dislocated his left elbow while trying to regain his balance after he was tripped by one of his own lineman in a 37-20 loss to the Cowboys. Daniels, the 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year, dislocated the same elbow last season, in which he appeared in only seven games due to multiple injuries. “It sucks for him,” Washington coach Dan Quinn told reporters Monday. “I know how much these guys put into it. So, when there are setbacks like this, you just want to stand by them.” A little before Daniels’ exit, the Bears’ Williams was carted off the field with a hamstring strain in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings. While Williams’ emotional exit from the game quickly became a social media meme, it also cut short what had been an exciting start to the season. Chicago was coming off a Week 1 in which it had scored 59 points. “He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here. We’ll see what that looks like,” Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. Johnson added that Williams has an ability to recover quickly, and his injury is considered week-to-week. While the Bears, Giants and the Commanders all lost after their starters went down, their seasons are far from over. The Vikings lost Murray in Week 1 but still managed a 2-0 start to the season with Carson Wentz at the helm. And now Murray is expected to start in Week 3 after recovering from a concussion. The Seahawks are also 2-0 with Drew Lock playing in place of Darnold, and even exploded for 31 points on Sunday. Darnold is expected to return to practice this week, though his starting status is up in the air. For now, the Bears will turn to Tyler Bagent, the Giants to Jameis Winston, and the Commanders to Marcus Mariota as the three clubs try to keep their seasons afloat without their young leaders. And Dart, Williams and Daniels — all three of whom have flashed potential to not only be great players but stewards for the league because of their exciting style of play — will have to wait a little longer to cement their star turns.

articles.title: Sean McVay Calls Himself a 'Dumbass Coach' in Joke About Rams' Australian Travel Plans
articles.summary: Most of the discussion around the Los Angeles Rams after their Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers was the team's travel plans for its trip to Melbourne.
articles.body:
Most of the discussion around the Los Angeles Rams after their Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers was the team's travel plans for its trip to Melbourne.

After beating the New York Giants on Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay called himself a "dumbass" when discussing his decision to give the team a late arrival to their international game.

"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spots," McVay joked.

The Rams looked much more like the team fans expected to see this year in a 28-6 win over the Giants, and they can now put their travel mistakes behind them and focus on the rest of the season.

articles.title: Los Rams olvidan Australia y se reactivan con la reaparición de Aaron Donald a costa de los Giants
articles.standfirst: Los Rams estuvieron liderados por Matthew Stafford
articles.summary: Los Rams estuvieron liderados por Matthew Stafford
articles.body: Los Ángeles Rams dejaron atrás la derrota sufrida en Melbourne (Australia) contra los San Francisco 49ers en la jornada inaugural de la NFL y se reactivaron con un contundente 28-6 a los New York Giants en el SoFi Stadium angelino. En un estadio eufórico por el regreso de Aaron Donald, por primera vez desde que anunció su retirada en 2023, los Rams se pasearon liderados por Matthew Stafford, que lanzó para 327 yardas, completó 22 de 31 envíos, dio cuatro pases de anotación y sufrió una interceptación. Davante Adams fue su principal socio, con ocho recepciones para 195 yardas y dos 'touchdowns'. Por tierra, encabezados por Kyren Williams, los Rams sumaron 163 yardas por las modestas 52 de los Giants. Los neoyorquinos llegaban a Los Ángeles tras una sólida victoria contra los Dallas Cowboys, pero su entusiasmo se cortó por completo en la primera posesión, cuando el mariscal de campo Jaxson Dart sufrió una peligrosa hiperextensión de la rodilla izquierda. Fue obligado a dejar el partido y no regresaría a competir. Eso sí, el 'QB' siguió el resto del encuentro en el banquillo, muchas veces de pie, una señal de esperanza para Nueva York. Le sustituyó Jameis Winston y sufrió ante la feroz defensa de los Rams. No pasó de las 111 yardas, con 11 de 27 en pases y fue interceptado una vez. Las únicas anotaciones de los Giants llegaron gracias al pie del pateador Dominic Zvada. Se jugó en un SoFi Stadium repleto, en el que Myles Garrett, dos veces mejor jugador defensivo de la NFL, estuvo en el palco mientras sigue con su proceso de recuperación por un problema de rodilla. Los Rams tampoco pudieron contar con su receptor estelar Puka Nacua, pero entre las estrellas presentes en los palcos estuvieron figuras de la NBA como Russell Westbrook y DeMar DeRozan, entre otros. La segunda semana de la NFL dejó un triunfo de carácter de los Kansas City Chiefs, que superaron en la prórroga a los Indianapolis Colts con un gol de campo definitivo de Harrison Butker. Patrick Mahomes lanzó para 347 yardas y tres pases de 'touchdown' para Kansas City. También fue una jornada marcada por lesiones, con Jayden Daniels retirado tras sufrir una luxación en el codo izquierdo en la derrota 37-20 de los Washington Commanders ante los Dallas Cowboys, y Caleb Williams abandonando el campo en camilla en el 9-3 de los Minnesota Vikings contra los Chicago Bears. Los Philadelphia Eagles remontaron para imponerse 24-20 a los Tennessee Titans con un pase decisivo de Jalen Hurts para Darius Cooper, mientras que los Baltimore Ravens cayeron 24-17 ante los New Orleans Saints. Seattle ganó 31-7 a Arizona y San Francisco venció 35-13 a Miami para mantener su pleno de victorias.
