articles.title: ‘The Super Bowl Favorite,’ ‘Not the Force We All Thought They Would Be’ — NFL Analysts Divided on Rams Despite MNF Win Over Giants
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams looked nothing like a Super Bowl favorite in Australia. Eleven days later, they looked much closer to the team many expected to see.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams looked nothing like a Super Bowl favorite in Australia. Eleven days later, they looked much closer to the team many expected to see.

The Rams beat the New York Giants 28-6 on Monday Night Football, with Matthew Stafford throwing for 327 yards and four touchdowns despite playing without Puka Nacua . Davante Adams erupted for eight catches, 195 yards and two scores, while Los Angeles held New York without a touchdown.

NFL Analysts Split on Rams After Dominant Giants Win

PFN's Kyle Soppe viewed the result as evidence that Week 1 deserves to be treated as the outlier.

Soppe wrote , "Goofy travel stuff is in the rearview. This team was the preseason Super Bowl favorite. This team deserves to be the Super Bowl favorite. The offense is explosive and it might be their second-best unit when at full strength."

Jacob Infante came away similarly impressed, especially by Adams.

Infante wrote , "As a Bears fan, I've seen my fair share of dominant Davante Adams performances. He was on another level tonight. The Rams bounced back in a major way on offense. This is what we expected them to look like."

Los Angeles' 15,000-mile trip to Australia was one of the NFL's strangest opening-week variables. The Rams were routed 27-7 by the San Francisco 49ers, and PFN's Team Impact Rankings reflected that opener before Monday's result, placing Los Angeles No. 32 with a 62.8 grade.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Rams Face Much Tougher Test Over Next 3 Weeks

Brandon Astreicher wrote , "Rams took care of business tonight. But I'm not so sure they're the force we all thought they would be yet. Broncos , Eagles, and Bills next up. If they win all three, then they're what we talked them up to be and my SB favorite again. Until then, they're just a good playoff team."

PFN's Brandon Austin pointed to New York 's injury situation, writing, "The Rams took care of business against a Giants team that played without Dart for most of the game. Still not sure what to make of them, but the talent on this roster is off the charts."

Jaxson Dart injured his knee on New York's opening possession and did not return. Jameis Winston replaced him, and the Giants never reached the end zone.

PFN's Zachary Knerr wrote in the aftermath, "Week 2 provided a nice bounce back for Los Angeles, but with the Seahawks firing on all cylinders with Lock under center it won't be as easy as we thought for Matthew Stafford and the Rams."

The upcoming schedule should settle the argument quickly. Los Angeles visits the Denver Broncos in Week 3, the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4, and then hosts the Buffalo Bills in Week 5.

Monday restored the version of the Rams that generated championship expectations all offseason. Whether it restored their status as the team to beat will require more than one dominant night against an injury-riddled opponent.

articles.title: Bengals’ Defensive Line Is Loaded, and Cedric Johnson Just Proved It
articles.summary: Sixth-round spark plug Cedric Johnson fueled a 41-pressure onslaught against Houston, proving Cincinnati’s relentless pass rush possesses the terrifying dept...
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals did it again in week two, showcasing their much-improved defensive line and securing their second straight win to start the 2026 NFL season.

Dexter Lawrence made a big 4th-and-1 stop, showing the game-wrecking ability that made the Bengals comfortable spending a first-round pick on the interior defensive tackle. Jonathan Allen had a tackle for loss, and the group posted a shocking 41 pressures, making Texans quarterback CJ Stroud uncomfortable all day.

However, someone far down the depth chart had a stellar day, showing the immense depth of the Bengals defensive line as a unit. Cedric Johnson posted five pressures, tying Jonathan Allen and Dexter Lawrence for third-most in Week 2. That trio trailed Cashius Howell, who had six, and Boye Mafe , who led the team with eight pressures.

Johnson is in his third year with the Bengals after being taken in the sixth round out of Ole Miss in the 2024 NFL Draft. He played in nine games in 2024 and 2025, totaling 27 tackles and three sacks. So far through 2026, Johnson has two sacks and five pressures on just 42 defensive snaps.

Johnson sacked Stroud to end the game this past Sunday in garbage time, chasing him backward as Stroud desperately tried to find a receiver. According to Joe Goodberry on X , Johnson had the highest pass-rush win rate of any Bengals player against the Texans at 26.3%.

Shemar Stewart told reporters on Monday that Johnson is playing "balls to the wall," and said Johnson didn't even know he had two sacks until he received a game ball in the postgame meeting.

Having a pool of pass rushers who can have success like Johnson, and thereby give rest to guys like Boye Mafe, Cashius Howell, Shemar Stewart , and Myles Murphy , is likely why the Bengals have been able to sustain the elite level of pressure from snap one to the final snap of the game through two weeks.

The level of play across the entire defense has made many people rethink what the Bengals can be as a team this season. Former NFL quarterback Alex Smith went on ESPN Monday and said they went into Houston and dominated the Texans, the week after the Bills got a ton of flowers for narrowly winning a high-scoring game.

Smith also noted that Burrow has been uninspiring , and that when he really turns it on, they could be one of the most dangerous teams in the league.

articles.title: How Giants' promising season changed in one nightmare game with Jaxson Dart, more injuries piling up
articles.summary: After their Week 1 win over the Cowboys, John Harbaugh and the Giants were flying high, but a rash of injuries to key players out on the west coast may have...
articles.body:
After their Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys , John Harbaugh and the New York Giants were flying high, and fans were dreaming of a revival.

In that season-opening win, all phases of the game looked polished and in midseason form. Second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart was nearly perfect at home in Week 1, with star receiver Malik Nabers returning from an ACL injury that ruined his rookie year looking his old self.

That had Giants fans dreaming of a return to form, having made the playoffs just once in the last nine seasons.

Then, it all seemingly came crashing down in one game on the west coast, with their season now hanging in the balance. Dart, who has struggled with injuries throughout his young career, suffered a knee injury, while Nabers himself picked up a shoulder injury that, while not keeping him out of the game, looked to limit him the rest of the way.

All told, the game would end in a 28-6 defeat, but beyond the final score, Giants fans will be waiting with baited breath on the injury status of multiple star players who dropped like flies at SoFi Stadium.

Will the Giants be able to work past the injuries to key players? Or has their season been sabotaged just when hope for better times finally seemed to be building?

Early in the Giants' second drive of the game, disaster struck as Giants star quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered an ugly injury that had every single New York fan holding their breath.

As Dart dropped back to pass on third down, he was sandwiched by two Rams pass rushers, hit first on his front side by Byron Young and then from the blind side by blitzing linebacker Josaiah Stewart . The initial hit by Young pushed Dart's lower half into the second hit by Stewart, whose upper leg made contact with the outside of Dart's knee.

The joint hyper-extended, and it left Dart clutching his knee in pain on the turf. Giants fans feared the worst for their star quarterback, who has been fantastic in his young career but has missed considerable time with injuries.

One positive seemed to come early in the second half, when ESPN sideline reporter Laura Rutledge said that Giants GM Joe Schoen told her that Dart "is going to be ok." That certainly sounds vague, but it at least seems to allay fears of a season-ending injury.

After the game, Ian Rapoport reported that Dart suffered a sprained MCL, and that he is "expected to miss some time," it's far from the catastrophic possible outcome of a more serious injury.

Additionally, head coach John Harbaugh said after the game that it was "in the vicinity of" an MCL sprain, and was "not a devastating outcome" for Dart, which is a sigh of relief for the Giants. The team will know more after further tests tomorrow, at which point they will have a better idea how long he will be out. There is still a chance he misses a significant chunk of time depending on the severity of the injury.

Regardless, they will have to navigate the time he is sidelined, with Jameis Winston under center.

On the final play of the first quarter, the nightmare continued for Giants fans as Malik Nabers suffered what appeared to be a shoulder injury on a seemingly innocuous play near the sideline.

An out route saw Nabers targeted by backup quarterback Jameis Winston just past the first down marker, but some hand fighting with Trent McDuffie saw the ball fall to the turf incomplete. Nabers immediately grabbed his left shoulder, in a ton of pain, eventually collapsing to the ground.

It was difficult to tell exactly what happened, as the replay didn't seem to show anything that would suggest an injury occurred. Nevertheless, the Giants were now potentially staring the loss of their star quarterback and superstar wide receiver both in the same quarter.

While Nabers would eventually come back into the game midway through the second quarter, he appeared to be limited. He was targeted on an interception thrown by Jameis Winston in the end zone, into the arms of McDuffie, and then did not appear on the field for any of the Giants next four plays in their ensuing possession.

He was in and out of the lineup, but did not have another catch for the remainder of the game.

After the game, Nabers said he dislocated his shoulder, and "popped it back in" on the sideline before returning to the game. He will get X-rays in the coming days to determine the extent of the injury.

In the fourth quarter, with the game seeming to slip away, pass rushing star Brian Burns saw his left ankle rolled up on chasing Kyren Williams on an end around.

He was in clear pain and could barely put any weight on it, needing help from trainers to limp off the field.

Fortunately for the Giants, Harbaugh told reporters after the game that Burns is believed to have suffered a low-ankle sprain, not the dreaded high-ankle sprain that typically costs players more time. Burns was reportedly spotted with a walking boot on his foot while exiting the stadium, and took a golf cart to the team bus.

When Brian Burns limped off the field in the fourth quarter, he was unable to get in the blue medical tent because it was already occupied by the team's undisputed leader of the offensive line, Andrew Thomas.

There was no indication exactly what happened to Thomas, but some eagle-eyed reporters claimed that he was slow to get up after a Jameis Winston fourth-down incompletion early in the fourth quarter.

Thomas would be listed as questionable to return with a groin injury, and would not return as the Rams kneeled out the game.

When John Harbaugh was asked about Thomas's injury after the game, he said that "we'll see about that one" and added "none of these injuries are life-threatening."
